newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy plans to cut national petrol station network.
newsitem.headline: Italy plans to cut national petrol station network.

text.p: Italy plans to trim its vast network of retail petrol pump outlets by some 5,000 over the next two years in a plan worked out this week by industry body Unione Petrolifera (UP).

The voluntary plan agreed with individual petrol companies and service station owners aims to thin out the national network by concentrating on closing the less efficient and poorly situated retail outlets.
The project envisages a scheme of incentives and compensation for the closure of outlets.
Italy has over 28,000 service stations, or nearly 10 per 100 square km, the largest network in Europe.
UP's project will now be submitted to the Industry Ministry and is expected to go before parliament as a bill in autumn.
UP chairman Pasquale de Vita said the move was a major step forward in streamlining the country's retail network. "We are trying to get Italy's network more in line with others in Europe."
Currently some 81 percent of Italian petrol station income came from fuel sales, eight percent from other services and just 11 percent from "non oil" sales.
This compared to a European average of 33 percent, 14 percent and 54 percent respectively.
De Vita said the project would allow petrol stations to diversify their range of services and therefore income.

"It is also in the interests of consumers because a network providing a wider range of services is also more economical from the management point of view," he said adding that the streamlining should eventually result in lower petrol prices.
